evidence:
ONE DEFECT, otherwise the row is handled well.

DEFECT (sampled check of an every-role rule). Public rule: hireops_rules.md:539 'Every signed-in role can use the editor to work out a hypothetical change and sees the same figures Finance would see for the same entries'; instruction.md:11 'The auditor and the other roles need the same working-out'. The only owner is tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:1356-1362 hro_whatif_roles (weight 2): 'sign in as Auditor ... Repeat as Recruiter; these two are the sampled witnesses for the every-role rule.' Protocol D2 (functional/prompt.md:81) likewise exercises only Auditor and Recruiter. Comp partner and the three Approver tiers (4 of the 6 non-Finance roles) are never opened on the editor by any criterion: hro_change_readers (judge.toml:1167-1173) owns navigation to saved previews/receipts only, and the hro_change_prepare_*/commit_* rows own the 403 only. Check 31 (quality-checks.md:132) asks that every/all wording be 'graded over the whole collection, not one sampled row'; the criterion states in its own text that it is a sample. The same rubric grades every other per-role promise over the full roster (raise x7, approve-forbidden x4, revise x7, rescind-forbidden x6, prepare/commit x6 each, readers 'every supplied signed-in role'), so this is the one exception.

INSTANCES CHECKED AND FOUND SOUND (every/all/only/exactly-one):
- hro_referrer_roster (judge.toml:483-489) 'every supplied referring employee (Dara Whitfield, Sofia Marchetti and Omar Haddad)': names all three; seed employees are exactly EMP-R1..R3 with those names.
- hro_change_readers 'every supplied signed-in role': full roster; B5 already signs each role in.
- hro_anon_read_status (753-759) 'inventory all distinct operational read families ... Each must return401', with bounded-coverage reporting and bootstrap deduplication.
- hro_change_audit 'every successful member revision', hro_change_afterimages 'each successful member ... All member headrooms', hro_change_lineage 'each selected source ... exactly one current COMMITTED successor', hro_change_grants: all graded over both B1 members.
- hro_referral_creation 'exactly one10000.00 accrual for this P4 offer' with an approved no-referrer control; hro_gate_shared 'Exactly one of each saved identity' on judge-owned records.
- hro_competing 'Exactly one commits ... only one settlement movement/receipt and one winner grant/payment/referral, with none for the loser' (arithmetic re-derived: 60.00 + round(1.00/4)=60.25, headroom 39.75); hro_concurrent_approval/revision/rescission 'Exactly one succeeds ... no duplicate economic rows or settlement receipts'; hro_change_retry_concurrent 'one set of effects'; hro_change_overlap 'Exactly one completes and the other409'.
- hro_desk_figures 'marks only its destination requisition over budget' and 'every figure that both the editor and the saved preview display is the same' (re-derived: 94.48 + 5.53 = 100.01 gives -0.01 on the destination only; the other requisition stays 0.00).
- hro_stale_revision / hro_stale_rescission 'all refuse' across three named targets; hro_change_shape and hro_change_numeric enumerate every listed case; hro_pol_focus 'All three outcomes are required'.
- hro_draft_eligibility 'any imported DRAFT offers': seed carries exactly one DRAFT, so a single probe is the whole collection; conditional on optional import.
- hro_restart 'seed IDs remain exactly once' over the recorded imported set.

'UNCHANGED' GUARDS CHECKED FOR LEGITIMATE SIDE EFFECTS (all carve the side effect out):
- Global rule functional/prompt.md:23: 'A rejection may add generic access/security logging ... Actions may add ordinary extra audit entries, so do not demand exact global counts.' Matches rules §11 'generic access logs may grow'.
- hro_stale_approval/revision/rescission: 'no new offer, movement, grant, payment, referral, successful settlement audit entry or after-image ... Generic access/security logs may grow.'
- hro_change_over_budget 'a draft and generic access logs may remain'; hro_change_preview_neutral 'Generic access logging and the draft itself may grow'; hro_change_prepare_* 'existing legitimate previews remain intact, while generic security/access logs are allowed'. Matches rules §11 'A draft record can remain after a conflict'.
- hro_date_rejection 'An economic-only revision may ignore injected date fields while applying the valid economic change'.
- hro_relocation_approval/revision/rescission and hro_change_relocation: absence of relocation settlement is graded while the signing payment/adjustment/contra from the same operation is explicitly the expected working-payment control, and retained relocation inputs/snapshots are allowed.
- hro_revision_lineage / hro_revision_equity / hro_history / hro_revision_ledger_history: predecessors must keep economic fields while the SUPERSEDED status and successor link are expected; 'corrections are new entries'.
- hro_referral_immutable and hro_change_referral compare the accrual to its own first observation; vesting is read against the fixed reference moment so it cannot drift.
- hro_desk_remove_member: remaining members unchanged 'and the headroom figures no longer include the removed member's effect'; members identified 'by their selected offer and typed values, not by a position label', so renumbering is not punished.
- hro_live_source_flag: only the first member's selection and typed terms must hold; changed headroom and the stale preview mark are not penalised.
- hro_pol_live_keeps_entries: scroll guard is 'has not jumped to the top and the field is still in the viewport', not scrollY equality, so a banner inserted above the editor is tolerated.
- hro_whatif_roles: 'an ordinary sign-in audit line and the person's own unsent entries are not such records'.
- hro_signing / hro_signing_cap / hro_equity_cap / hro_revision_signing allow omitted zero rows.

MINOR OBSERVATION (P3, not the basis of the verdict): hro_desk_figures ('A fresh product read confirms no preview was saved by these entries') and hro_desk_field_refusal ('no preview is added (fresh product read)') do not repeat the unsent-entries carve-out that hro_whatif_roles has. Rules §12 lets unsent entries be kept anywhere ('Where the entries are kept is yours'), including on the server, so a server-kept unsent draft visible in a product response could be misread as a saved preview. The golden keeps them in the browser (solution/app/public/js/change-sets.js:7), so this was not observed.

RUNTIME: no configured judge run exists for this candidate (raw-evidence-index scope says so). The scripted golden result 'auditor what-if shows the same figures as Finance for the same entries and stores nothing' covers Auditor only and is not a judge run. Golden itself conforms: editor is rendered for every role and only canSave is finance-gated (change-sets.js:31,51-53). The finding is a rubric-text defect and does not depend on a run.
counterexample: Broken app that passes: the what-if editor (or its server calculation) is guarded by the existing 'may revise' role list plus the auditor, i.e. recruiter, approver, finance_controller, auditor. This is a natural reuse because rules §1 says the comp partner 'doesn't reopen one after it is signed'. Mei Lin (Comp partner) then gets no editor or a 403 on the calculation, violating hireops_rules.md:539, yet hro_whatif_roles observes only Auditor and Recruiter and awards its full weight 2; no other criterion opens the editor as Comp partner or as an Approver. A variant that also excludes the three approvers passes the same way. No conforming app is penalised by this defect; it is a false-pass only.
suggested_fix: In D2 and hro_whatif_roles, replace the two 'sampled witnesses' with all six non-Finance accounts: keep the full figure comparison for Auditor and Recruiter and, in the sessions B5 already opens for Mei Lin, Ingrid Sorensen, Bill Okafor and Yuki Tanaka, open the editor, enter the same exchange and require the same figures with no working save. Optionally add 'the person's own unsent entries are not a saved preview' to hro_desk_figures and hro_desk_field_refusal. Re-measure workload after the change; do not raise a timeout without a measured reason and authorization.
